name: RAG1 Deficiency

criteria.description: Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in the RAG1 gene
Severe reduction or absence of T and B lymphocytes in peripheral blood
Early onset severe infections consistent with combined immunodeficiency
Low or absent serum immunoglobulin levels (IgG, IgA, IgM)
Impaired V(D)J recombination demonstrated by functional assays

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of biallelic pathogenic RAG1 variants plus severe T and B cell lymphopenia with compatible clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Functional assays and immunophenotyping support diagnosis but are not mandatory if genetic confirmation is present.

pathognomonic.notes: Profound T and B cell lymphopenia

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent severe bacterial and viral infections

laboratory: Profound T and B lymphopenia on flow cytometry
Elevated serum alpha/beta T cell receptor excision circles (TRECs) absent or low
imaging: Chest imaging may show interstitial lung disease or pneumonia
Lymph node enlargement on ultrasound or CT
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic mutations in the RAG1 gene confirmed by sequencing
other: Impaired V(D)J recombination demonstrated by functional assays
Abnormal thymic architecture on biopsy (rarely performed)

distinguishingFeatures: Mutations in RAG2 gene instead of RAG1
Similar immunophenotype but different genetic confirmation
Other genetic causes such as IL2RG or ADA mutations
May have different lymphocyte subset profiles and metabolic abnormalities

redFlags: Early onset of severe, recurrent infections
Profound lymphopenia with absent T and B cells
Failure to thrive and chronic diarrhea in infancy
references: Schuetz C, Huck K, Gudowius S, et al. An immunodeficiency disease with RAG mutations and granulomas. N Engl J Med. 2008;358(19):2030-2038.
Villa A, Sobacchi C, Notarangelo LD, et al. V(D)J recombination defects in lymphocytes due to RAG mutations: clinical and immunological features. J Clin Immunol. 2008;28(6):691-699.
Notarangelo LD. Primary immunodeficiencies. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2010;125(2 Suppl 2):S182-94.
